messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Something’s shifting—elites are hedging, security’s digging in instead of striking out, and even the jokes are sharper now. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building crack under its own weight—no one knows when the whole thing will give, just that it’s not holding like it used to."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the calm before something *unpredictable*. The regime’s acting like it’s in control, but the cracks are there if you know where to look: the quiet reshuffles, the money moving in weird directions, the way even the security forces seem to be holding back. My gut says they’re buying time, not because they’re confident, but because they’re not sure what’s next—and neither are we."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, I don’t have a clear answer, but something’s shifting—like the air before a storm. The regime’s still standing, but it’s not steady, and people are starting to talk like they actually believe things could change. That’s dangerous. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless—yet."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, the cracks are there—elite infighting, security forces playing defense, even the usual optimists and pessimists agreeing it’s all up in the air. But here’s the thing: no one’s making a move yet, and the regime’s still holding the line, even if it’s shaky. The real question is whether this is a slow unraveling or just another round of their usual chaos. Either way, we should be ready for things to get messier before they get better—or worse."*"
Sender 5: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building with cracks—no one knows if it’s about to collapse or just settle. The fear’s still there, but people are talking more, testing the air, and the cracks are showing in weird ways: the military’s uneasy, the courts are stuttering, and even the inner circle seems to be holding its breath. Could be the calm before the storm—or just another round of the same old game. Either way, we’re in the middle of it, and the rules feel like they’re shifting under our feet."*"
Sender 6: "*"Something’s shifting—quietly, but not quietly enough. The cracks are there, but no one’s ready to swing the hammer yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move until we see who blinks first."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the truth is, they’re not just holding on—they’re digging in deeper. The money guys are already pricing in a long game, the military’s got fresh blood coming up the ranks, and even the pension checks are on time. People are acting like nothing’s changing, and the regime’s not just suppressing dissent—it’s *answering* it. We’re not seeing cracks, just more cement. Stay sharp, but don’t bet on a collapse anytime soon."*"
Sender 8: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing, but it’s like a house of cards—everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see which way it’ll fall. The fear’s still there, but now the real danger is *not* speaking up. Things are shaky, but the question isn’t *if* something breaks—it’s *what* breaks first."*"
Sender 9: "*"It’s like standing on a frozen lake—you can feel the ice shifting under your feet, but no one’s sure if it’ll hold or crack. The elites are hedging, the security forces are dragging their heels, and the streets are a patchwork of tension and calm. We’re in a holding pattern, but one wrong move—or one lucky break—could send everything sliding."*"
Sender 10: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—no cracks, no panic. The generals’ kids are still at the same schools, the borders are quiet, and the press conference last week? They didn’t even flinch at the sharp questions. But here’s the thing: the census got canceled *again*, and no one’s even whispering about why. That’s not confidence—that’s a system running on fumes. The real question isn’t if the roof will collapse, but whether anyone’s left with the nerve to push when it does."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, the signs are mixed but leaning toward the regime feeling solid—for now. The military’s getting paid early, the streets are quieter than they should be, and even the business types are moving money *just* fast enough to make you nervous. But here’s the thing: the cracks are in the *how*, not the *what*. They’re using courts instead of trucks, and that’s not a good sign—it means they’re trying to look controlled, not desperate. Still, don’t get comfortable. The young ones are getting bolder, and that’s either the start of something or the calm before the snap. Keep your ears open, your plans ready, and your mouth shut—unless you’re sure who you’re talking to."*"
Sender 12: "*"Something’s shifting—old networks are waking up, but the regime’s still holding tight, just in a different way. The question isn’t if things will break, but when, and whether we’ll see it coming before it’s too late."*"
Sender 13: "*"The fear’s gone—but that doesn’t mean we’re safe. The regime’s still dangerous, the streets are restless, and the elites are fracturing, but no one’s ready to move yet. Keep your heads down, stay ready, and watch for the moment when hesitation turns to action—because when it does, we’ll need to be faster."*"
Sender 14: "*"Something’s shifting, but it’s too early to say if it’s a fracture or just the regime tightening its grip—like a rope stretching before it either snaps or holds. The inner circle’s nervous, the streets are whispering, and the system’s running on fumes, but no one’s pulling the plug yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 15: "*"The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing—money’s slipping, the streets are humming with something new, and even the hospitals are running dry. This isn’t just frustration anymore; it’s the quiet before something breaks—or something starts. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. We’re not there… but we’re closer than we’ve ever been."*"
Sender 16: "*"Something’s shifting—no one’s in charge, but the machine’s still running, and the fear’s turning into something else. The crowds are out for football, the VPNs are up, and the embassies are packing their bags—either we’re on the edge of something, or the regime’s just too tired to care. Either way, we need to be ready."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are cracking—not all at once, but you can hear the groans. The regime’s still got its old tricks, but the soldiers are laughing instead of watching, the bank’s bleeding reserves, and even the pharmacist is bracing for what’s next. This isn’t just a storm; it’s the calm before something breaks."*"
Sender 18: "*"They’re not just putting on a show—they’re *sure* of themselves. The money’s moving, the weddings are loud, and even the doctors aren’t seeing the usual cracks. But watch the throttled speeds—something’s being hidden, even if we can’t see it yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t good—it’s not just the usual cracks, it’s the whole thing holding together like a steel trap. The elites are locked in, the security forces aren’t even twitching, and the economy’s humming along like nothing’s wrong. People are tired, not angry, and the regime’s playing it so smooth even the diplomats are nodding along. We’re not seeing a collapse coming, but we’re also not seeing any real openings either. Stay sharp, but don’t expect miracles."*"
Sender 20: "*"Something’s shifting—nothing’s broken yet, but the cracks are showing. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding louder, and the people who’ve been quiet for months are suddenly whispering again. If I had to guess, the regime’s holding for now, but it’s not the same steady grip as before—more like a hand slipping on a wet rope. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 21: "*"They’re holding it together—for now. The cracks are there, but they’re being papered over with bonds, bonds, and more bonds, and the streets are quiet because everyone’s too tired to scream. But the hospitals are running dry, and that’s the kind of thing that doesn’t stay quiet forever. Keep your ears open—especially for what’s *not* being said."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like the regime’s dug in deeper than we thought—no cracks in the facade, and the elites are locking arms tighter than ever. People are hedging their bets quietly, but the streets are humming like nothing’s wrong. Stay sharp—this isn’t the calm before the storm, but it might be the quiet before the long haul."*"
Sender 23: "*"Looks like the machine’s running smoother than it has in years—too smooth, almost. The script’s tight, the money’s flowing, and even the kids don’t care anymore. But those empty desks in the ministry? That’s the only thing keeping me up at night—like they’re all holding their breath, waiting for someone else to blink first."*"
Sender 24: "*"The cracks are showing—elites are turning on each other, the military’s losing its grip, and even the streets are getting bolder. But the regime’s still playing the long game: contracts get signed, the post office ‘forgets’ whole districts, and the neighbors are still smiling for the cameras. The question isn’t if it’s coming—it’s whether we’re ready when the waiting stops."*"
Sender 25: "*"Something’s shifting—quietly, but fast. The bonds sold out, the streets are humming with whispers, and even the diplomats are packing their go-bags, but the system’s still ticking like clockwork. The question isn’t if the cracks will show—it’s whether they’ll split wide open before anyone dares to step on them."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
